title: Erdős #1054 OQ-01: The Sum-of-Divisors Function is Always Representable
description: Generalizes Construction D (Erdős #1054) from case-by-case native_decide checks to a single axiom-free theorem: for every m ≥ 1, the sum of divisors σ(m) = ∑_{d∣m} d is representable, because it is always the LAST partial sum of m's sorted divisor list. This subsumes the parent's prime-square witnesses (σ(p²)=1+p+p²) and the entire Mersenne family (σ(2^k)=2^{k+1}-1) without the Lean.ofReduceBool axiom, and adds a prime-power corollary that ∑_{i=0}^k p^i is representable for every prime p.

meta.author: Lean Genius Researcher
meta.assumptions: None. All seven theorems are fully machine-checked and depend only on the standard foundational axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. In particular, NO native_decide is used, so the results are free of Lean.ofReduceBool — a deliberate strengthening of the parent file, whose concrete witnesses (constr_d_*, mersenne_repr_*) rely on native_decide. axiomCount=0.

mathlibDependencies.description: The sorted divisor list is a permutation of the divisor finset, so their sums agree (sortedDivisors_sum).
The last entry of scanl (·+·) 0 L equals foldl (·+·) 0 L, i.e. the running total — the crux that identifies the final partial sum with σ(m).
∑_{d∣p^k} d = ∑_{i=0}^k p^i, giving the prime-power geometric-sum corollary.

mainTheorems.name: sum_divisors_representable
mainTheorems.description: The sum-of-divisors function σ(m) is representable for every m ≥ 1, witnessed by m itself.
mainTheorems.significance: Single axiom-free theorem subsuming every concrete representability check in the parent file — the structural reason all of them hold.

mainTheorems.name: sum_divisors_mem_partialSums
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ m ≥ 1, (∑ d ∈ m.divisors, d) ∈ partialDivisorSums m
mainTheorems.description: σ(m) is the LAST partial sum of m's sorted divisor list — the running total of all divisors.
mainTheorems.significance: The key structural insight: representability of σ(m) is automatic, not a coincidence to be checked case by case.

mainTheorems.name: geom_sum_representable
mainTheorems.statement: ∀ p prime, ∀ k, IsRepresentable (∑ i ∈ range (k+1), p^i)
mainTheorems.description: Every geometric sum 1 + p + ⋯ + p^k for a prime p is representable (witness p^k), since it equals σ(p^k).
mainTheorems.significance: Generalizes the parent's prime-square family (k=2) and Mersenne family (p=2) into one axiom-free statement.

mainTheorems.name: prime_sq_sum_representable'
mainTheorems.description: Recovers the parent's Construction D headline as the k=2 instance, now without native_decide.
mainTheorems.significance: Re-derives a previously native_decide-flavoured result in fully verified form.

mainTheorems.name: mersenne_representable
mainTheorems.description: Recovers the Mersenne family (∑ 2^i = 2^{k+1}-1 = σ(2^k)) without native_decide.
mainTheorems.significance: The infinite Mersenne family of representable numbers, axiom-free.
